correctness.rationale: For identical G, if A_i=B_i, the signed local field requires all neighbors in both layers to share that pair, so connectedness forces exactly two fully aligned configurations. Otherwise B=-A globally, and both signed fields equal d-2r_i+a; d-2<a<d is positive exactly when r_i<=d-1. For prisms, the 16-state overlap transfer is a bijection with non-singleton binary words, its exact integer characteristic polynomial is checked from its explicit matrix by verify.py, and Rouche on |z|=2 establishes one dominant real root in (3,4). Full microscopic enumeration checks four graphs; this is supportive and not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary full text establishes only two homogeneous opposed absorbing configurations, not a complete intermediate-coupling microscopic classification or exact prism entropy. A separate published stronger-coupling involution is confined to a>d, and a published prism Lucas census treats an uncoupled one-layer majority map. Exact no-singleton partition language and classic threshold-period statements were compared at implication level; no reviewed source supplies this specific theorem. A previously unknown equivalent graph-coloring census remains a historical-priority risk, not a mathematical inference of coverage.
residual_risks: Classical constrained-coloring or zero-temperature Ising ladder work could encode the quartic count under another terminology; available indexed searches and source checks do not exhaust historical literature.
The 1980 general threshold paper was not available in complete full text; its accessible high-level eventual-period theorem is not the present exact enumeration.
Independent priority and proof review have not been performed.

value.rationale: The main source foregrounds two homogeneous opposed outcomes and simulation-defined metastability. The complete intermediate-coupling theorem reveals a structural family of frozen spatially nonuniform configurations and classifies all of them for arbitrary connected regular identical layers. The exact prism quartic establishes exponential absorbing-state entropy for a natural cubic contact network, demonstrating mathematically how extensive microscopic frozen heterogeneity can coexist with simple macroscopic polarized states; it is not an arbitrary isolated parameter slice or merely a code check.
